articles.title: Fossilised red blood cells found in 115m-year-old dinosaur’s bone, say scientists
articles.description: Chemical tests on Aratasaurus bone identify presence of heme, the organic compound that allows haemoglobin in blood to carry oxygen around body It could be the opening of a Jurassic Park rip-off: scientists examining ancient dinosaur bones find what appear to be fossilised red blood cells, and traces of the molecule that gives the beast’s blood its distinctive crimson hue. But that is what researchers are claiming to have discovered after analysing the hind leg bones of a small, meat-eating dinosaur called an Aratasaurus that lived and died in what is now north-eastern Brazil 115m years ago. Continue reading...

articles.title: How a scientist went from hero to traitor in a US water crisis – podcast

source.name: Presented by Ian Sample, produced by Joshan Chana, sound design by Joel Cox, the executive producers were Madeleine Finlay and Ellie Bury

articles.description: When the water in Flint, Michigan, became contaminated with dangerous levels of lead, Dr Siddhartha Roy, then a third year PhD student, was part of the team of scientists who publicly contradicted state and federal claims that it was safe. He became a local hero until a new piece of research challenged the idea that children in Flint had been left permanently brain damaged by the crisis. His adherence to the evidence, no matter who it offended, has earned him the 2026 Maddox prize, which recognises individuals who stand up for science and evidence, despite challenges or hostility. He tells Ian Sample how he reflects on his experience in Flint, and why he lost friends as a result of his work there Read more Guardian coverage of the Flint water crisis Support the Guardian: theguardian.com/sciencepod Continue reading...

articles.title: Tributes paid to ‘inspiring’ Cambridge scientist who died in Spain train crash
articles.description: Dr Marta Shahbazi was travelling to a conference to receive award for scientific excellence in developmental biology An “inspiring” Cambridge scientist died in the Spanish train collision on Wednesday that killed at least 69 people.
